findings.who: A partner or S corporation shareholder whose 2025 Schedule K-1 reports a net section 1231 gain or loss because the entity sold a rental building or business equipment. Neither spouse sold anything personally.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you (or ... your spouse)' sold or traded property. The entity sold it, so the truthful answer is no. The help never mentions sales passed through on a K-1.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Use Form 4797 to report the following. 1. The sale or exchange of: a. Real property used in your trade or business; b. Depreciable and amortizable tangible property used in your trade or business'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'or did a Schedule K-1 you (or your spouse) received report a section 1231 gain or loss, or a sale of business or rental property by the partnership, S corporation, estate or trust?' Route a yes to the Form 4797 refusal.

findings.who: A filer who sold or exchanged section 1244 small business stock or section 1242 SBIC stock at a loss in 2025, or whose such stock became worthless.
findings.why_no: Stock is neither real estate nor 'business property' as the help defines it. Worthlessness is also not a sale or trade. Even if the filer reached the child question, it says to count only property 'not held as an investment', which excludes this stock.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Form 4797 list: '4. Ordinary loss on the sale, exchange, or worthlessness of small business investment company (section 1242) stock. 5. Ordinary loss on the sale, exchange, or worthlessness of small business (section 1244) stock.'
findings.fix: If no other question already refuses these losses, ask: 'Did you sell stock at a loss, or have stock become worthless, in a small company you bought shares in directly when it was formed or raised money?' Route a yes to the Form 4797 refusal.

findings.who: A securities trader who made a mark-to-market election and has 2025 gains or losses on securities held in the trading business.
findings.why_no: The help's examples of business property are 'equipment, a vehicle or a building'. A trader would not see stocks and options as 'business property', so the trader answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Form 4797 list: '6. Ordinary gain or loss on securities or commodities held in connection with your trading business, if you previously made a mark-to-market election.'
findings.fix: Ask separately: 'Have you (or your spouse) made a mark-to-market election as a trader in securities or commodities?' Route a yes to the refusal.

findings.who: A farmer or rancher who sold cattle, horses or other livestock held for breeding, dairy, draft or sporting purposes, or sold standing timber or timber cut under a section 631 election.
findings.why_no: The help lists 'equipment, a vehicle or a building' as examples, and the filer reads that list as complete. Animals and trees do not look like 'business property' or 'real estate' to them.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: Form 4797 reports 'b. Depreciable and amortizable tangible property used in your trade or business' and '3. The disposition of noncapital assets other than inventory'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Business property also includes livestock kept for breeding, dairy, draft or sport, standing or cut timber, and farmland improvements made with government cost-sharing payments.'

findings.who: An owner of a single-member LLC or a revocable living trust that holds title to a rental house, business equipment or the main home, where the LLC or trust is the named seller on the 2025 deed or Form 1099-S.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you' sold the property. The LLC or trust is the seller on the paperwork, so the filer believes they did not sell it.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1: 'Real property used in your trade or business'; p. 2: 'Report the sale or exchange of your main home on Form 8949 if: ... You received a Form 1099-S for the sale or exchange.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Count property sold by a single-member LLC you own or by a living trust you set up and control, as if you sold it yourself.'

findings.who: A filer who sold a co-op apartment that was their main home and received a Form 1099-S, or whose gain exceeded the exclusion.
findings.why_no: A co-op owner holds shares in a housing corporation, not a deed. The filer may think they sold stock, not 'real estate'. The help's 'a home you lived in' may not settle that.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 2: 'Report the sale or exchange of your main home on Form 8949 if: • You can’t exclude all of your gain from income, or • You received a Form 1099-S for the sale or exchange.'
findings.fix: Change the help to: 'Real estate includes any home you lived in as your main home, including a co-op apartment (shares in a housing cooperative), a condominium, a mobile home or a houseboat.'

findings.who: A filer whose main home was a mobile home, manufactured home or houseboat that is not titled as real property, sold in 2025 with gain beyond the exclusion.
findings.why_no: The home is titled like a vehicle, so the filer thinks it is not 'real estate'. It was not used in a business either, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 2: 'Any gain you can’t exclude is taxable.'
findings.fix: Use the same broadened help wording as the co-op finding.

findings.who: An employee who took depreciation in an earlier year on a personally owned car or equipment used for their job, and sold or traded it in during 2025.
findings.why_no: The help says business property is 'anything used in a business'. A W-2 employee does not think of their job as 'a business'.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Form 4797: 'Depreciable and amortizable tangible property used in your trade or business'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Include anything you ever took depreciation on or deducted for business use, including use in your job as an employee.'
